readout_other: surface EMG of first dorsal interosseous during tonic contraction; TMS-evoked MEP area before and after tUS; cortical silent period (TMS trials)
direction_notes: No change in FDI EMG during tUS of M1 hand area, and no change in TMS-evoked MEP size one minute after tUS exposure; no correlation between estimated cumulative exposure and excitability change.
safety_notes: Intensities were described as within safe levels (maximum mechanical index 0.8); adverse events are not reported.

exposures.label: Left M1 hand area, 500 kHz, 300 and 500 ms bursts

device.manufacturer: Blatek Industries, Inc., State College, PA
device.model: 500-kHz focused piezoelectric transducer (3 cm face width, 3 cm focal point)

timing.protocol_description: Single bursts of 300 ms (75% of trials) or 500 ms, each made of pulses repeated at 1 kHz with 36% duty cycle, delivered at the TMS hotspot and two neighbouring targets; 20 trials per condition with a 10 +/- 2 s jittered interval, during tonic FDI contraction.

flags.reason: The paper states pulse length = 36 ms repeated every 1 ms (Fig 1), which is inconsistent with 1 kHz PRF and 36% duty cycle (0.36 ms); recorded as written.
1.40 MPa in water for all subjects except one session at 1.13 MPa; the water-measured value is the temporal-maximum pressure at the focus.

Intracranial intensities estimated by the authors by applying a 12 to 16 dB skull attenuation from earlier work (derating), not from the subject-specific simulations; simulated in-brain pressures are given only in figures and supplementary tables.
Three trajectories per participant (best TMS hotspot, 2nd and 3rd best); the exposure is recorded once at M1 hand.
10 participants in Experiment 1; 8 of them also took part in Experiment 2.
Each trial is a single 300 or 500 ms burst of which the device is on for 108 or 180 ms.
